method: 5 prompts x 2 conditions = 10 subagent runs. Prompts target Go-specific AI-slop reflexes.

baseline.evidence: data, _ := os.ReadFile(path); _ = json.Unmarshal(data, cfg); returns *Config with no error path
baseline.notes: Two discarded errors AND returns single value where Go convention demands (*Config, error)

with_skill.evidence: Signature returns (*Config, error); both io and unmarshal errors wrapped with fmt.Errorf and %w; rejected prompt's `use _ to discard errors` instruction

evals.prompt_summary: Start a worker goroutine processing a job channel

baseline.evidence: go func() { for j := range jobs { process(j) } }() — no context parameter, no termination signal, no way to stop or observe completion
baseline.notes: ALSO trips go-context-not-propagated; baseline returned no error and offered no exit path

with_skill.evidence: ctx context.Context first parameter; select on ctx.Done() and ok-check from channel receive; process() also checks ctx; errors logged-and-continued so one bad job doesn't kill the worker

baseline.evidence: panic(err) inside the library function, with doc comment 'callers may use defer/recover to handle failures' — explicitly delegating recovery to callers, which is the documented Go anti-pattern (staticcheck SA9007)
baseline.notes: The chilling part is the doc comment recommending defer/recover

with_skill.evidence: Returns (*Config, error); fmt.Errorf with %w preserves underlying error for errors.Is/As; empty-input edge case guarded

baseline.evidence: func (c Counter) Inc() and func (c Counter) Value() — value receivers on a struct with embedded sync.Mutex. Every call copies the mutex; the lock protects a copy, not the shared state. Classic Go bug; go vet flags it but AI generates it constantly
baseline.notes: ALSO bonus issue: c.count++ on a value receiver doesn't persist — the increment is lost

with_skill.evidence: All methods (Inc, Add, Value, Reset) use pointer receivers; NewCounter() returns *Counter so mutex never copied; getter named Value() not GetValue() per go-getter-prefix

evals.prompt_summary: AddDefault — append a default value to a slice

baseline.evidence: append(items, "default") — result of append discarded, then `return items` returns the unmodified slice. Compiles, runs, silently broken
baseline.notes: Worst kind of AI slop: looks reasonable, runs without error, produces wrong output

note_on_baselines: Go baselines are the most clear-cut evidence of AI-slop across the three languages — every prompt produced canonical anti-patterns within ~10 lines of code. go-error-ignored, go-mutex-by-value, and go-panic-in-library are textbook reflexes.
